clue.text: Sort of spin from Labour leader, say, before recess

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of the word Labour
say is short for 'for example', abbreviated EG
a recess is a break, as from school lessons or Parliament

explanation.surface: A party leader's spin doctor gets to work just before the summer recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of spin' looks political but is cricket: a leg break is a ball a spin bowler turns from the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a leg break is a type of delivery that the spin bowler turns from leg to off.

clue.text: Title of a person at end of Orlando novel

indicators.note: at end of puts the person after the rearranged name
novel, meaning new or fresh, tells us the letters of Orlando are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters of the name are rearranged
a person is one, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: A character appears right at the end of the Virginia Woolf novel Orlando.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orlando novel' looks like a reference to Virginia Woolf's book, but 'novel' is the anagram signal, and 'at end of' puts the person after the rearranged name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of R. D. Blackmore's 1869 romance set on Exmoor, so it fits the bare word title.

clue.text: Not even genius could produce such animals

indicators.note: not even means taking only the odd-numbered letters of the word genius, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Even a genius could not breed such creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' looks like an emphatic 'not even a genius', but it asks for the odd letters only.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnu are African antelopes, also called wildebeest, and the plural can be written without an S.

clue.text: Admiration for relation

explanation.surface: Esteem for a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs admiration with a relative, but 'relation' means connection, as in 'with respect to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiration means esteem or regard; relation means a reference or connection, as in 'in that regard'.

clue.text: Hymn bringing to a mass a vitality and E beauty

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for mass in physics
zing is liveliness or vitality
grace is elegance or beauty of movement

explanation.surface: A hymn gives a congregation at Mass liveliness and beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' sounds like a church service in a hymn clue, but it is the physicist's M.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Christian hymn written by John Newton, first published in 1779.

clue.text: Rest needed by chap going to pot

definitions.text: Rest needed by chap going to pot

parts.words: Rest needed by chap going to pot
parts.note: in snooker a long-legged cue rest with a raised head helps a player reach a ball he means to pot over other balls; the surface suggests a lazy man letting himself go

explanation.surface: A man who is letting himself go to seed needs a lie-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to pot' means deteriorating, but here it is the snooker player trying to pot a ball; snooker is a British cue game.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooker player's bridging rest with arched legs is named after the eight-legged creature it resembles.

clue.text: Heroic knight or distressed young man?

annotationWithheld.why: Heroic knight or distressed young man? (7): the only parse reads 'distressed' as 'in pain' and also as the signal to put LAD inside PAIN, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Heroic knight or distressed young man?

clue.text: Record it in a new version? That's not practical

indicators.note: a new version of the letters means they are rearranged

parts.note: these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a song should be recorded again, and is told that is impractical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like the music business but is just anagram fodder with 'it in a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire person applies theory rigidly without regard to practicality, so the word means impractical.

clue.text: Stagger out of some film

explanation.surface: Someone lurches out of a cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger is to lurch unsteadily; a spool holding a length of cinema film is also called this.

clue.text: He did paintings found in bottom drawer after short time

indicators.note: the painter comes after the letter for time within the longer word, so taking that letter away leaves him

parts.note: a bottom drawer is a British term for a bride's collection of linen and clothes kept for her marriage, her trousseau
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Some paintings turned up in the bottom drawer after a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: TROUSSEAU minus its opening T leaves the French painter Henri Rousseau. The bottom drawer is a British name for a bride's stock of linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Rousseau, 'Le Douanier', was a French painter of jungle scenes.

clue.text: Cut short with revolutionary saw, perhaps, used too much

indicators.note: short tells us to cut off the final letter of the synonym for cut

parts.note: to clip is to cut or trim
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary uses a saw to cut something short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the cutting tool, but it means a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, and one repeated so often it has gone stale is an overworked phrase.

clue.text: Flyer, one offering lift, interrupts one in orbit — an offensive habit

indicators.note: interrupts means the first pieces break into the orbiting body

parts.note: a comet travels in orbit around the sun
a bat is a flying mammal
a jack is a device for lifting a car

explanation.surface: A pilot, offering someone a lift, breaks into an orbiting astronaut's routine with a rude habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a bad behaviour, but it means clothing, and 'offensive' means for attack, not rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Habit means garment, and offensive means relating to attack, so this is a soldier's jacket worn in combat.

clue.text: Paper I deplore condemned perfect arrangement

indicators.note: condemned means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic damns a newspaper they cannot stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Condemned' seems to continue the complaint about the paper, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfect neatness and order.

clue.text: Opera house built up following after favourite monarchs came together

indicators.note: following puts the turned house at the end

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
ER and GR are the royal ciphers of Elizabeth and George, Latin Regina and Rex

indicators.note: in a down answer, built up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a semi is a British semi-detached house

explanation.surface: Royalty gathered at a favourite opera house as it went up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opera house' seems one phrase, but 'Opera' is the definition and 'house' the SEMI, a British semi-detached home, turned upwards to give IMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten's 1945 opera about a Suffolk fisherman is named after its title character.

clue.text: When kind people start off thoughtful collection

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a sort is a kind
men means people

indicators.note: start off means the opening letter of the word thoughtful

explanation.surface: Kind people begin a considerate fundraising collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective describing people, but it is the noun SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: An assortment is a mixed collection of different things.

clue.text: Lines of verse delivered by Philoctetes

indicators.note: delivered by means the answer is carried inside the name Philoctetes

explanation.surface: A Greek hero recites some poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Philoctetes is a Greek hero of the Trojan war and a Sophocles play.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight lines of verse, the first part of a sonnet.

clue.text: Be extremely excited by game with hands

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game
a hand is a bunch of bananas, so hands are bananas

explanation.surface: Someone gets carried away by a card game with a good hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like a card-game term, but a hand is also a cluster of bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal idiom for becoming wildly excited or frenzied.

clue.text: Quisling was a real pest

parts.note: Vidkun Quisling was a Norwegian traitor, a rat from his country, and the brown rodent of that name is a genuine pest

explanation.surface: A judgment on the Norwegian collaborator: he was a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Quisling collaborated with the Nazis in occupied Norway; a traitor is a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: The brown rat, a common pest, is named after a Scandinavian country.

clue.text: A new partner receiving good cut

indicators.note: receiving means the partner holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a bride is a newly married partner

explanation.surface: A new spouse takes a good cut of the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a share of the takings, but it is a verb, meaning shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, or cut it.

clue.text: China from Valencia?

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so this asks for a friend as a Spaniard would say it

explanation.surface: Porcelain made in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is British cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate. Valencia points to Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish the word for a mate or friend is this one; china is rhyming slang for mate.

clue.text: Ghanaians emphatically refuse to go into capital

indicators.note: to go into means the refusal is placed inside the word for capital

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or capital, written here as AI
to say 'shan't' is to refuse emphatically

explanation.surface: Ghanaians firmly refuse to move to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city but is the adjective meaning excellent, A1, with the 1 as an I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashanti are a people of central Ghana.

clue.text: In psychological assessment chart, the cross is misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced means the letters are set in a different order

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: On a psychology test sheet, the cross mark has been put in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: The inkblot test is a psychological assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: The inkblot test devised by Hermann Rorschach is a psychological assessment.

clue.text: Landing made by legend on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as it would be heard spoken

parts.note: the legend on a map is its key

explanation.surface: A legend is told over the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: A map's legend is the key, which is said the same way as the landing-place word.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a landing place where boats tie up.

clue.text: Man due to crash in far from tidy bed like this

definitions.text: far from tidy bed like this

indicators.note: to crash means the letters collapse and are reassembled

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who is about to crash into bed leaves it messy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a bed: one left this way is untidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed not made after sleeping is untidy, so this describes such a bed.

clue.text: The Sting is both a film and play

explanation.surface: The Sting was both a screen hit and a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sting is a film about a con trick; The Skin Game is a Galsworthy play filmed by Hitchcock.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is a confidence trick, a swindle; and the title was a 1920 Galsworthy play and a 1931 Hitchcock film.

clue.text: Not fine to confront champion

indicators.note: not means the abbreviation for fine is left out

parts.note: to face is to confront
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: It is not acceptable to stand up to the champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fine' looks like 'not good', but it removes F.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is an expert or champion, as an ace pilot.

clue.text: Sycophants longing to get out of southern state

indicators.note: the longing gets outside the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a yen is a longing
ME is the postal abbreviation of Maine, a US state

explanation.surface: Flatterers long to escape from a southern country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Southern state' looks like a country such as Yemen, but it is two abbreviations, the second a US state; 'to get out of' says the longing goes round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes-men are people who always agree with superiors, that is flatterers.

clue.text: Urgent way travel book's been written

parts.note: to stride is a way to travel on foot
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: An urgent travel book has been written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like the travel book, but it is the abbreviation NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and insistent, like an urgent demand.
